title: Choose ShellFlow's look
question: The roll assigned Chop & Seal. The layout you know stays the same in every option; only the look changes. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Chop & Seal
options.lineage: Company chops, embossed common seals and stamped approval papers
options.thesis: Every cleared gate and every approval is stamped on the record, the way MFE already signs paper.
options.viewport: The same header and two-row step menu; each cleared step carries a small dated cinnabar chop, and the valuation panel carries an embossed seal.
options.risk: Overused, the chop turns into decoration; it may only appear where an approval or gate really happened.

raised.raise: Each of the eight steps owns one ink from a fixed set, used identically on its tab, page band and records.
Every block wears the same name plate on every page: block code, start date and a one-line status.
Every record carries a fixed reference number, such as MR11-STP2-B04, set the same way everywhere.
Every grey comes from one fixed tonal ramp, and a conflict shows a pattern as well as a colour.
A changed figure keeps its revision mark until the person responsible has seen it.

options.label: Tower Lobby
options.lineage: Lobbies of the finished towers: honed limestone, brushed bronze, lift floor indicators
options.thesis: The system wears the finish of the buildings MFE delivers; the current step glows like a lift's floor number.
options.viewport: The same header and step menu set as a bronze directory board, the active step lit amber like a lift indicator, forms on pale stone cards.
options.risk: Bronze and stone is where most 'luxury' screens land, so it can read as a hotel rather than as MFE's own system.

options.label: Transit Line
options.lineage: Enamel metro maps: coloured lines, station ticks, interchange rings
options.thesis: The eight steps drawn as one line; each block is a train at its station, and the 4-Way gate is the interchange.
options.viewport: A midnight enamel header with the step menu drawn as a line of stations; work areas on porcelain white.
options.case: Fuses cleanly, since steps really are stations, but MFE staff know their chop and seal better than a metro map.
options.risk: A dark shell over long working days, and the line crowds the menu on phones.

options.label: Tabbed Manual
options.lineage: Boxed software manuals with coloured divider tabs
options.thesis: Each page a divider in its own full-strength hue, the tabs stepping down the edge.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail replacing the step menu.
options.case: Loses both: staff do not know these manuals, and a new tab rail moves the menu they learned.
options.risk: Changes the navigation people already know.
options.kept: One fixed ink per step, used identically everywhere.

options.label: Gate Board
options.thesis: Lorries and blocks ranked like departures, changes flashing in place.
options.viewport: Every page as a departures board.
options.case: Loses both: it suits Logistics but not forms, workbooks or approvals.
options.risk: Fits one department, not sixteen pages.
options.kept: A changed figure stays marked until someone has seen it.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.lineage: Record-label catalogue numbers on matte black sleeves
options.thesis: Everything numbered, names replaced by code.
options.viewport: A black field with one plot and a catalogue number.
options.case: Loses both: coded labels slow down people who read numbers all day.
options.kept: A fixed reference number on every record.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.lineage: Darkroom printing records and zone ramps
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over an eleven-step tonal ramp; hatching shows load and conflict.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets sliding over the work area.
options.case: Loses both: no link to MFE's work, and sliding sheets replace the familiar page.
options.risk: Unfamiliar movement on a working screen.
options.kept: One fixed tonal ramp; conflict shown by pattern, not colour alone.

options.label: Character Roster
options.thesis: Every block a character card with a name plate and a birthday.
options.viewport: A pastel roster grid of blocks.
options.case: Loses both: playful, and wrong for a luxury operations brief.
options.kept: The same name plate for a block on every page.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What top operations software ships, executed impeccably: white, slate greys, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: The same header, menu and form, in the familiar enterprise look at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other systems by design; the luxury lives only in finish.
